question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Parallel & Intersecting Lines (Angles & Linear Pairs)

questions.question_text: If two straight lines intersect and one angle is 45°, what is its vertically opposite angle?
What is the maximum number of intersection points for two distinct straight lines?
The sum of measures of angles forming a linear pair is:
Two intersecting lines form angle x and angle y as a linear pair. If x = 2y, find x and y.
Define parallel lines and state their key distance property.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Parallel lines lie in the same plane and never intersect regardless of extension. The perpendicular distance between them remains constant throughout.

questions.question_text: In an intersection of two lines forming clockwise angles a, b, c, d, if a = 35°, find b, c, d.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: b = 180° - 35° = 145° (linear pair). c = a = 35° (vertically opposite). d = b = 145° (vertically opposite).

questions.question_text: Architects design a window grid where vertical frame line V is perpendicular to horizontal sill line H. Diagonal support brace D crosses the intersection at 35° to line H. Calculate all four angles formed around the intersection.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Angle 1 = 35°. Angle 2 (linear pair) = 180° - 35° = 145°. Angle 3 (vertically opposite to 1) = 35°. Angle 4 (vertically opposite to 2) = 145°.

questions.question_text: Explain how paper folding can be used to construct parallel and perpendicular line creases step by step.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Fold square paper in half horizontally to make crease L1. Fold in half again horizontally to make creases L2, L3. Unfold to see parallel horizontal lines. 2. Fold sheet vertically across horizontal creases to create a perpendicular line crease P1 forming 90° right angles with all horizontal creases.

questions.question_text: Perpendicular lines intersect at what angle?
If angle A and angle B form a linear pair and angle A = 115.3°, find angle B.
Which real-world object represents parallel line segments?
If one angle of two intersecting lines is 90°, prove that all four angles are 90°.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Let a = 90°. Linear pair b = 180° - 90° = 90°. Vertically opposite c = a = 90°. Vertically opposite d = b = 90°. All four angles equal 90°.

questions.question_text: Distinguish between intersecting and parallel lines.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Intersecting lines meet at exactly one common point. Parallel lines lie in the same plane and never meet at any point.

questions.question_text: Two adjacent angles on a straight line are (3x + 10)° and (2x + 20)°. Find x and the measure of each angle.

A road intersection has two straight crossing streets A and B. Traffic police measure one corner angle to be (4x - 15)° and the adjacent corner angle to be (x + 20)°. Determine x, calculate all four corner angles, and check vertically opposite equality.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Linear pair sum: (4x - 15) + (x + 20) = 180° => 5x + 5 = 180° => 5x = 175° => x = 35°. Angle 1 = 4(35) - 15 = 125°. Angle 2 = 35 + 20 = 55°. Angle 3 (vertically opposite to 1) = 125°. Angle 4 (vertically opposite to 2) = 55°. Checks: 125 + 55 = 180°; vertically opposite angles are equal.

questions.question_text: Prove that if two lines intersect, the vertically opposite angles are equal using the linear pair axiom.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Let lines l and m intersect forming angles a, b, c, d in order. 1. a and b form a linear pair: a + b = 180°. 2. b and c form a linear pair: b + c = 180°. 3. Equating both sums: a + b = b + c. Subtracting b from both sides yields a = c. Thus vertically opposite angles a and c are equal.

questions.question_text: If two lines are perpendicular to the same line, what is the relation between them?
Angle supplementary to 72° is:
Angles in a linear pair are always:
Find the angle which is equal to its supplement.
If two vertically opposite angles are (2x + 10)° and (x + 35)°, find x.
Three lines intersect at a single common point. How many vertically opposite angle pairs are formed?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 3 lines intersecting at one point form 6 angles. Total vertically opposite pairs = 3 pairs.

questions.question_text: A fence design features two parallel horizontal wooden rails R1 and R2 crossed by vertical posts P. Explain why all intersection angles formed by P with R1 and R2 are right angles (90°).
questions.marking_scheme_answer: If post P is perpendicular to R1, it forms 90° angles. Since R1 and R2 are parallel, post P crosses R2 at the exact same inclination angle. Thus, all 8 angles around both intersections with R1 and R2 equal 90°.

questions.question_text: Four ray lines OA, OB, OC, OD meet at point O in clockwise order. If angle AOB = 80°, angle BOC = 100°, angle COD = 80°, prove whether lines AC and BD are straight lines forming vertically opposite angles.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Check angle AOB + angle BOC = 80° + 100° = 180°. Since adjacent angles sum to 180°, AOC forms a straight line AC. Check angle BOC + angle COD = 100° + 80° = 180°, so BOD forms a straight line BD. Since AC and BD are straight intersecting lines, angle AOB (80°) and angle COD (80°) are vertically opposite and equal.

Complement of 35° is:

Find the supplement of 135°.
An angle is 20° more than its supplement. Find the angle.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Let angle be x. Supplement = 180° - x. Equation: x = (180 - x) + 20 => 2x = 200 => x = 100°.

questions.question_text: In a figure, two lines AB and CD intersect at O. If angle AOC = 50°, find angle AOD and angle BOD.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: angle AOD = 180° - 50° = 130° (linear pair). angle BOD = angle AOC = 50° (vertically opposite).

questions.question_text: A steel bridge truss contains two parallel chord beams connected by diagonal struts forming angles with the chord. If one interior angle is 65°, find all remaining three angles at that junction.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Angle 1 = 65°. Angle 2 (linear pair) = 180° - 65° = 115°. Angle 3 (vertically opposite) = 65°. Angle 4 (vertically opposite to 2) = 115°.

questions.question_text: Draw/Describe the grid dot paper test to verify whether two given line segments on a dot grid are parallel.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Count grid units: measure vertical rise and horizontal run between grid dots for segment 1. Measure rise and run for segment 2. If the ratio of rise to run is identical for both segments, they maintain constant inclination and constant perpendicular distance, proving they are parallel.

Linear pair angles ratio is 2:3. Find smaller angle.
If ratio of linear pair angles is 2:3, find both angles.
Can two obtuse angles form a linear pair? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: No. An obtuse angle > 90°. Sum of two obtuse angles > 180°, which violates the 180° linear pair rule.

questions.question_text: If angle A = 25°, find its complement and its supplement.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Complement = 90° - 25° = 65°. Supplement = 180° - 25° = 155°.

questions.question_text: In an intersection of two lines, the sum of two vertically opposite angles is 140°. Find the measure of all four individual angles at the intersection.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Let vertically opposite angles be a and c. Since a = c and a + c = 140°, 2a = 140° => a = 70° and c = 70°. Linear pair angle b = 180° - 70° = 110°. Vertically opposite angle d = 110°. The four angles are 70°, 110°, 70°, and 110°.

questions.question_text: A solar panel array tilt mechanism uses two crossed support arms pivoting at center point O. Prove that adjusting the tilt angle on one side creates an identical tilt angle on the opposite side.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The crossed arms form two intersecting straight lines. The angle of inclination on one side and the angle on the opposite side are vertically opposite angles. Since vertically opposite angles are always equal by geometric proof, changing the angle on one arm automatically alters the opposite angle by the exact same amount.

question_papers.paper_title: Class 7 Mathematics Model Test Paper - Chapter 5: Parallel and Intersecting Lines

questions.question: When two straight lines intersect, what is the measure relationship between vertically opposite angles?
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Vertically opposite angles are equal: angle a = angle c and angle b = angle d. [1 Mark]

questions.question: What is the sum of two adjacent angles forming a linear pair on a straight line?
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Linear pair angles are supplementary and sum to 180°. [1 Mark]

questions.question: What is the key defining property of parallel lines in a plane surface?
options: A) They intersect at right angles
B) They maintain constant perpendicular distance and never meet
C) They meet at exactly two points
questions.correct_answer: B) They maintain constant perpendicular distance and never meet
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Parallel lines remain equidistant and never cross regardless of extension. [1 Mark]

questions.question: If two lines intersect at 90°, what type of lines are they?
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Lines intersecting at right angles (90°) are perpendicular lines. [1 Mark]

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Two distinct straight lines in a plane can intersect at most at one unique point.
Reason (R): If two straight lines shared two distinct points, they would coincide and form the exact same line.
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.correct_answer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.marking_scheme_solution: A fundamental geometric postulate states two lines intersect at most at 1 point. [1 Mark]

questions.question:
Assertion (A): If angle a = 35° at an intersection, then its linear pair angle b = 145°.
Reason (R): Angles forming a linear pair lie on a straight line and sum to 180°.
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.correct_answer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.marking_scheme_solution: 35° + 145° = 180°. R provides the linear pair definition. [1 Mark]

questions.question: If two lines intersect and one angle is 45°, calculate its vertically opposite angle and its adjacent linear pair angle.
questions.marking_scheme_solution:
Vertically opposite angle = 45°. [1 Mark]
Linear pair angle = 180° - 45° = 135°. [1 Mark]

questions.question: Two intersecting lines form angle x and angle y as a linear pair. If x = 2y, calculate the exact values of x and y.
Explain how successive parallel horizontal paper folds generate parallel line creases.
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Folding paper in half repeatedly aligns opposite edges, producing crease lines that remain equidistant and parallel to top and bottom edges. [2 Marks]

questions.question: Prove why vertically opposite angles angle b and angle d are equal when two lines intersect.
questions.marking_scheme_solution:
Angle b and angle a form a linear pair: b + a = 180°.
Angle d and angle a form a linear pair: d + a = 180°.
Equating both: b + a = d + a => b = d. [2 Marks]

questions.question: Why might two non-intersecting line segments drawn on a sheet of paper NOT be parallel?
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Line segments may not meet within a small page, but if their perpendicular distance varies, extending them further will cause them to intersect. To be parallel, they must be equidistant when extended infinitely. [2 Marks]

sections.section_name: Section C (Long Answer Questions / Numerical Proofs)

questions.question:
Two lines intersect forming four angles a, b, c, d in clockwise order. Given that angle a = 35°:
(i) Calculate angle b with geometric justification.
(ii) Calculate angle c with geometric justification.
(iii) Calculate angle d with geometric justification.
questions.marking_scheme_solution:
(i) angle b = 180° - 35° = 145° (Linear Pair Postulate). [1.5 Marks]
(ii) angle c = 35° (Vertically Opposite Angle Theorem: c = a). [1.5 Marks]
(iii) angle d = 145° (Vertically Opposite Angle Theorem: d = b). [1 Mark]

questions.question:
A window frame design has horizontal line H and vertical line V meeting at 90°. A diagonal support brace D crosses the intersection at 35° to line H.
(i) Find all 4 angles formed between brace D and line H.
(ii) Find all 4 angles formed between brace D and line V.
questions.marking_scheme_solution:
(i) Angles with line H: 35°, 145°, 35°, 145°. [2 Marks]
(ii) Angles with line V: Since H ⊥ V (90°), complement angle = 90° - 35° = 55°.
  Four angles with V = 55°, 125°, 55°, 125°. [2 Marks]

questions.case_scenario:
Case Study: Architectural Truss & Road Junction
Civil engineers design a steel bridge truss where diagonal support beams cross at major nodes.

sub_questions.sub_q: (a) Identify the vertically opposite pairs among angles 1, 2, 3, 4 formed at a beam crossing.
sub_questions.solution: Vertically opposite pairs: (Angle 1, Angle 3) and (Angle 2, Angle 4). [1.5 Marks]

sub_questions.sub_q: (b) Identify all linear pairs formed at the intersection node.
(c) If Angle 1 measures 115.3°, calculate the exact values of Angle 2, Angle 3, and Angle 4.
sub_questions.solution:
Angle 2 = 180° - 115.3° = 64.7°. [1 Mark]
Angle 3 = 115.3° (vertically opposite to Angle 1). [1 Mark]
Angle 4 = 64.7° (vertically opposite to Angle 2). [1 Mark]
